newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Verplaetse to replace Duisenberg as BIS president.
newsitem.headline: Verplaetse to replace Duisenberg as BIS president.

text.p: Alfons Verplaetse, governor of the Belgian National Bank (BNB), will replace Wim Duisenberg, president of the Dutch central bank, as the next president and chairman of the Bank for International Settlements (BIS).
BIS, central bank to the worlds' central banks, said on Monday its board of directors elected Verplaetse as president and chairman for period of three years starting on July 1.
Duisenberg's term at BIS was due to expire at the end of June when he takes over as president of the European Monetary Institute (EMI), the forerunner of the European Central Bank (ECB).

Under Duisenberg, BIS -- the worlds' oldest international financial institution -- moved rapidly to boost its global presence and last year it added nine new central banks to the 32-member organisation.
The nine new members are Russia, China, India, Hong Kong, Singapore, South Korea, Saudi Arabia, Brazil and Mexico.
Verplaetse, 67, was named governor of the Belgian central bank in July 1989 following his appointment as director of the central bank in 1985.
Between 1982 and 1988, he was also director of the Cabinet of the Belgian prime minister, where he played a key role in the recovery of the Belgian economy.

For many years Verplaetse was also member of the working group of monetary experts that reported monthly to the Committee of Governors of the Central Banks of the Member States of the European Community, based at BIS.
Last month Verplaetse was re-appointed for a limited one year period as governor of the Belgian central bank because he has passed the official retirement age.
His term at BNB is expected to be extended again next year, but it is widely anticipated that he will retire by February 1999.
If Verplaetse were to retire from the Belgian central bank before the end of his three-year term at BIS, he would also have to step down from his position at BIS.
Duisenberg, who also will be retiring from the Dutch central bank on June 30, has been president of BIS twice, the first man to hold the position for two terms.

BIS's board of directors is made up of central bank governors from the Group of 10 (G10) leading industrial nations, who meet to discuss international monetary and financial issues at BIS's tower-like headquarters in Basle 10 times a year.
